rubric.why: Burning magnesium produces a bright white flame and magnesium oxide.
rubric.description: States an observation or identifies the product formed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the dazzling white flame or for formation of white magnesium oxide.

modelAnswer: Magnesium burns in oxygen with a dazzling white flame.
A white powder of magnesium oxide is formed.

rubric.why: Sodium is used in lamps that provide bright light for streets.
rubric.description: Gives one use of sodium in lamps or street lighting.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for sodium-vapour lamps or street lighting.

rubric.why: Liquid sodium transfers heat in some nuclear reactors.
rubric.description: Gives a second use of sodium as a coolant in nuclear reactors.

modelAnswer: Sodium is used in sodium-vapour lamps for street lighting.

items.followUp: Define dipole-dipole forces and state how they affect boiling points.

rubric.why: The definition identifies hydrogen bonded to a highly electronegative atom.
rubric.description: Identifies hydrogen bonded to an electronegative atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the hydrogen is bonded or attached to an electronegative atom.

rubric.why: Hydrogen bonding is the attraction to a lone pair on an electronegative atom of another molecule.
rubric.description: Describes the intermolecular attraction to a lone pair on another molecule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying attraction to a lone pair on an electronegative atom of another molecule.

rubric.why: Extra energy is needed to overcome hydrogen bonds, raising phase-change temperatures.
rubric.description: States that hydrogen bonding raises melting or boiling points.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that hydrogen bonding raises or increases the melting point or boiling point.

rubric.why: Hydrogen bonding strengthens attractions between molecules and affects liquid properties.
rubric.description: States an increase in surface tension or viscosity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that hydrogen bonding increases surface tension or viscosity.

rubric.why: The open structure formed by hydrogen bonds makes ice less dense than liquid water.
rubric.description: States that ice is less dense than liquid water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for comparing the density of ice with that of liquid water.

modelAnswer: Hydrogen bonding is the intermolecular attraction between a hydrogen atom covalently bonded to a highly electronegative atom (N, O or F) and a lone pair on an electronegative atom of another molecule.
These attractions are relatively strong, so extra energy is needed to separate the molecules; consequently, hydrogen bonding raises melting and boiling points.
It also increases properties such as surface tension and viscosity.
In ice, hydrogen bonds form an open structure, making ice less dense than liquid water.
